items.title: sq-7d3dj.30.18: perf(engine): hoist rhs scans/builds across seed blocks in eval_bgp_binary_capped
items.body:
sq-7d3dj.30.8 v1 re-derives the GOO chain per seed block, so each non-bind step re-runs its rhs scan_to_bindings (and hash build) per block — bounded at ~3x by the three-block schedule (1024/64k/rest), paid only by ASK-false / LIMIT-miss queries. Hoist: derive the step order once, materialise each step's rhs once, reuse across blocks (hash tables reusable if build side is pinned to rhs — order-relaxed is fine, the capped contract is multiset-level). Composes with the stream_pipeline block driver design (research/lazy-pull-incremental-emission.md, sq-7d3dj.34.2.3) — consider sharing that machinery instead of a private hoist.

<!-- bd-id:sq-7d3dj.30.18 -->
Parent: #2588

items.title: perf/soundness: sibling result-serialisation paths (CSV/TSV/XML, CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE, QueryResult term materialisation) still lack a post-serialization budget gate
items.body:
sq-yfcu2 closed the hole for the general multi-pattern SELECT-JSON path in `sparq-engine::exec::eval_select_json_emit`: the budget now bounds the SERIALIZE step (mid-serialize re-check + post-serialization `budget::check`), so a deadline that falls due while an already-materialised result is being written out is reported as the budget error instead of being answered with a complete-but-late body.

The same class of hole appears to remain on the sibling paths, which also do unbounded work AFTER the last cooperative check:
- `sparq-server`'s CSV / TSV / XML result serialisers (`crates/sparq-server/src/results.rs`) — they serialise a materialised `QueryResult` with no budget visibility at all.
- `construct_ntriples_with_budget` / `describe_*_with_budget` — template instantiation + N-Triples serialisation after the final row gate.
- `eval_select`'s `QueryResult` build (per-cell `oxrdf::Term` materialisation) after `budget::check(rows.len())`.

Each is a behaviour change for late-but-complete results (same trade-off sq-yfcu2 accepted), so they want their own bead + acceptance test rather than being folded into this PR.

items.title: perf(engine): bind_join can now declare sorted_by on the join variable
items.body:
sq-7d3dj.7 made `bind_join` emit its output in contiguous runs of ascending join-value id, so `out_rows` IS sorted on the join variable's column (= `out_vars[rk]`). It still returns `Bindings::unsorted`, so downstream merge-join eligibility is left on the table.

Claiming the sortedness requires two things this PR deliberately did not do: (a) drop the `presorted` no-sort shortcut (or prove every producer of `Bindings::sorted_by` orders ASCENDING by id, since a stale/descending `sorted_by` would make the claim false rather than merely splitting runs), and (b) re-verify the suites that a newly-eligible merge join would now take. Worth measuring — it is free ordering information that currently gets discarded.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #3190. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
<!-- sparq-followup:v1 -->

items.title: perf(engine): batched bound scans across a run of bind_join join values
items.body:
sq-7d3dj.7's roadmap entry describes two changes; only the first landed. The run grouping is in (`FxHashMap<Id,Vec<usize>>` -> sorted index permutation + contiguous runs), and because the distinct values now arrive in ascending id order the per-value `store.scan` probes walk the chosen permutation forwards. But it is still ONE `store.scan` per distinct value, each paying a fresh `Perm::choose` + binary-search bound pair.

The remaining idea is a batched/multi-key bound scan: for a run of adjacent join values, resolve one range over the permutation index and split it, amortising the permutation choice and narrowing each successive binary search to the tail of the previous one. That needs a new `sparq-core::store` API, so it is a separate, cross-crate task.

items.title: perf(engine): preserve repeated-variable semantics and budgets in indexed top-k recovery
items.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

Two executed regressions block adoption of the indexed top-k optimization proposed in [PR #5983](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/pull/5983), head `59bfc6c44b25a4e107d5d957ca3287ba0bc22c1a`. This is an unmerged candidate defect: current main `cf19a52c6880c496cefaca24046174902bc30958` retains the existing evaluator.

**Repeated-variable semantics.** For this data:

```turtle
<urn:s> <urn:p> 1 .
```

this query must return no rows:

```sparql
SELECT ?x WHERE { ?x <urn:p> ?x } ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1
```

Importing the PR's exact two-file top-k delta onto current main returns `?x = <urn:s>`. The paired full-ORDER-BY control passes; the LIMIT regression fails. Restoring exact main's `exec.rs` makes both tests pass. The indexed path bypasses the generic evaluator's repeated-position equality enforcement.

**Intermediate resource limit.** Using the PR's existing 40-task claim-query fixture, `query_with_budget` with `max_rows: Some(2)` and `LIMIT 1` returns a successful result through the imported path instead of the expected intermediate-row limit error. The test failed at this first assertion, so that raw run does not establish what its later byte-limit assertions would do. The new scan/probe path bypasses the existing intermediate-budget accounting.

A local Astra recovery at `803bb795201782551d984221a48b32ed391f7d9c` reuses the existing repeated-variable shape guard, declines immediately when a query budget is active, and delegates multi-valued probes to the existing evaluator. Historical Luke Dary / Sonnet5 attribution is retained; only the new repair/tests are Astra work. PreparedGraphApplier and transaction retry helpers are outside this recovery slice.

Executed with pinned Rust/Cargo 1.97.1, offline and locked, default engine features, two build jobs and one test thread:

- Raw import: paired repeated-variable tests 1 pass / 1 fail; exact-main fallback 2 pass.
- Raw intermediate-row-budget regression: 1 assertion failure.
- Repaired focused suite: 19 pass, including row/byte/generous-budget and multi-valued fallback cases; existing ORDER BY suites: 17 pass.
- Six calibrated guard/engagement controls all fail a test, with no survivors or compile/harness errors.

Acceptance before landing: complete the remaining bounded ordering/view/resource cases, retain a demonstrably engaged fast path and correct fallback, obtain real independent Opus review, and provide reproducible measurement evidence before making performance claims. No latency improvement, full-workspace validation, independent approval or merge readiness is claimed by this issue. No release, registry dispatch or EC2 action was performed.

items.title: sq-7d3dj.27: perf(engine): lazy single-pattern scan for streaming SELECT-JSON — iterate the scan and push per 64KiB instead of materialising the Cow range (the TTFB headline for dump exports)
items.body:
Wave D child D4 of research/wave-d-pull-streaming-response-body.md (design sq-7d3dj.13) — the TTFB headline. single_pattern_scan_json currently materialises the whole scan range (Scan::rows: Cow<[[Id;3]]>) before serialising, so first-byte waits on the full range. Make it ITERATE the scan and push each ~JSON_CHUNK_BYTES chunk through the D1 sink as scanned, so TTFB drops to first-chunk time on the export shape (bare SELECT ?s ?p ?o, LIMIT-less dumps). Serial by nature (index order, incremental) — does NOT use the sq-7d3dj.10 parallel serializer (disjoint code path: parallel serialize applies to the materialised Bindings path, lazy scan to the single-pattern path — complementary, not competing). Range-prune / inline-filter passes preserved so byte-order matches the general path exactly. CRATE: sparq-engine (crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs). INVARIANT: byte-identical output vs the materialising path (differential guard); zk-recording + empty-default-view fall-throughs unchanged. ACCEPTANCE: on the bare-scan export the TTFB series (sq-7d3dj.23, EC2 canonical) drops toward first-chunk time and peak RSS toward O(chunk); byte-identity differential passes; clippy -D warnings + tests green in both feature states. [OPUS-4.8]

items.title: sq-7d3dj.33.2: perf(engine): bind-join / sideways-information-passing — seed BGP scans from a tiny VALUES join side instead of full-scan + hash-join
items.body:
From the sq-7d3dj.33 profile (research/shacl-baseline-2026-07.md §3): the executor evaluates Join(BGP, Values(k rows)) by materialising the FULL BGP result and hash-joining — a 1-row VALUES ?this { <iri> } next to a 2-pattern BGP costs ~464us on LUBM(1) (full predicate scans via PermData::rows_in) when an index-seeded evaluation would be ~us. FIX DIRECTION: in sparq-engine exec (eval_graph_pattern_inner / the conjunctive flattening), when one join side is a small materialised Bindings (VALUES or an already-evaluated tiny side), bind its variables into the BGP triple-pattern scans (index lookups per binding row, i.e. a bind-join) below a cardinality threshold; cost-gate so large VALUES keep the hash-join. Benefits: SHACL sh:sparql per-focus path (even unbatched), params-feature prepared-query rebinding, any VALUES-seeded query. Measure with the sq-7d3dj.33 probe shape + existing operator benches; no regression on the canonical suites.

<!-- bd-id:sq-7d3dj.33.2 -->

items.title: sq-7d3dj.30.16: perf(engine): correlated/capped OPTIONAL right side under ASK/LIMIT — avoid full right evaluation in the capped LeftJoin arm
items.body:
sq-7d3dj.30.8 v1 boundary: try_capped's LeftJoin arm caps the LEFT side (sound: OPTIONAL never drops a left row) but still evaluates the RIGHT side in full, so ASK { A OPTIONAL { huge } } pays the whole right relation. Options: (a) evaluate right correlated on the capped left's join keys (SIP-style seeding, then left_outer_join against the restricted right — restriction must be exactly join-key-compatible rows so unmatched left rows still extend with unbound correctly); (b) compose with the stream_pipeline block driver once sq-7d3dj.34.2.3 lands. Revert-witness idea: budget-bounded ASK over OPTIONAL with a huge right side.

<!-- bd-id:sq-7d3dj.30.16 -->
Parent: #2588

items.title: sq-7d3dj.30.19: perf(engine): compose value-join (sq-7d3dj.30.7) with the capped conjunctive driver so ASK q12a fully collapses
items.body:
sq-7d3dj.30.8's eval_bgp_binary_capped treats a cross-component equality FILTER as a residual over the per-block (cross-product) chain — correct but still pays the per-block cross join. sq-7d3dj.30.7 (value-join feature) unifies FILTER(?a=?b) across disconnected components into a value-keyed hash join, but only on the FULL eval_graph_pattern_inner path (eqjoin::try_eq_component_join). Compose: under the value-join feature, let try_capped's conjunctive arm attempt the component join capped (cap the probe side / drive the smaller component in blocks), so ASK q12a becomes first-match-in-first-block. Both parents merged first; keep the capped contract (sub-multiset + fewer-than-cap == complete).

items.title: sq-6i40: Local adaptive optimisation REDESIGN: pruning/strategy-aware runtime correction (not divergence-triggered arm-swap) — the path to an actual local perf win (sq-p6p6 follow-up)
items.body:
Follow-up to sq-p6p6 (#903/#948 CLOSED — the naive divergence-triggered fedplan port is perf-neutral on the local engine because local per-pattern estimates are EXACT, so GOO is already well-ordered and reordering only flips multiplicative arms).

The candidate for a REAL local win is a PRUNING-aware adaptive step, NOT an arm-swap: push the observed (materialised) per-variable distinct counts into the BIND-JOIN eligibility threshold / the decision to switch a join strategy (hash vs bind/index-nested-loop) mid-plan, where a wrong estimate actually costs real work that a runtime correction can recover. Design-first: identify the operator-level decisions in exec.rs where exact-estimate assumptions break (e.g. correlated predicates, FILTER selectivity, OPTIONAL/MINUS) and where runtime cardinality changes the OPTIMAL operator — those are the only places a local adaptive step can pay. Opt-in, default-off; benchmark-gated on a CANONICAL host (sq-0g6g); must show a real win on a realistic workload before landing. [OPUS-4.8]

<!-- bd-id:sq-6i40 -->

items.title: sq-3m7qw: perf(engine): condition cs-anchor-incidence prune on an extra bound probe position
items.body:
Follow-up from sq-jnb1e / PR #1836. The cs-anchor-incidence prune fires only when the probe pattern constrains ONLY the projected predicate and the join variable (probe id-pattern all-unbound). A probe with an EXTRA bound position (e.g. ?person ?predicate <const>) currently DECLINES the prune (unconditioned incidence over the whole predicate would be unsound: a predicate could relate an anchor member on a DIFFERENT triple than the one satisfying the bound constraint). This bead adds a CONDITIONED incidence set keyed by the extra bound (position, id) so those shapes can also be pruned. Must stay result-identical + differential-verified (the probe_with_extra_bound_position_declines test currently asserts on==off via decline; extend to assert the conditioned prune fires and matches). Lower priority — q09 does not need it.

<!-- bd-id:sq-3m7qw -->

items.title: sq-21my6: perf(engine): incremental maintenance of cs-anchor-incidence metadata under updates (remove the overlay-decline)
items.body:
Follow-up from sq-jnb1e / PR #1836. The opt-in cs-anchor-incidence prune (SP2Bench q09) currently DECLINES on any graph with a pending-update delta overlay (has_overlay()), falling back to the exact block scan — the derived incidence set is built against the base index only and incremental maintenance is out of scope for the initial slice. This bead adds incremental maintenance so the prune stays active after an UPDATE: on INSERT add the (predicate, position) to the incidence set for any affected anchor type; on DELETE conservatively invalidate only the affected (predicate, position) entries (a delete may remove the LAST member relation, so a naive keep is unsound — must re-verify or drop-and-recompute lazily). Must stay result-identical and differential-verified against the exact path including delete-then-query. Relates to the overlay merge substrate in sparq-core. Opt-in, keep core lean.

<!-- bd-id:sq-21my6 -->
